lede: A RealNVP posterior on full MNIST digits reconstructs softly and samples every class. The same fit on Fashion-MNIST keeps the garment and drops the print.
points: VAE · normalizing flow in the latent space
title: f-VAE
question: Does a RealNVP inside the VAE latent space improve reconstruction and likelihood on digits?
process: The encoder proposes a Gaussian, four coupling layers warp it, and the decoder reads the flowed code. KL is a Monte Carlo estimate of that RealNVP posterior against N(0, I). ELBO is the negative of the training objective. Bits per dimension use the Gaussian decoder that matches the squared error. Reconstruction grids decode the flowed posterior mean. The sample grid decodes draws from N(0, I), not an inverse through the flow: the flow is inside the posterior. Both runs use latent 32, hidden 256, 4 flows, and the official 60,000 / 10,000 split. Fashion uses the digits hyperparameters for 20 epochs. There is no second Optuna search and no Optuna plot.

opening.summary: Test MSE is 0.0554 and test ELBO is −69.35, essentially the same as train. Prior samples are soft digits from many classes. The flow’s test log-det is −12.87, so it is changing volume rather than sitting at the identity.
opening.hover: Hover a row for the number behind that sentence.

marks.label: Reconstruction
marks.summary: Test MSE 0.0554 and MAE 0.0920. Train is 0.0555 and 0.0923. The flowed posterior mean keeps the digit and softens the stroke. This is a full 60,000-image run at latent 32, so it is not the same setup as the latent-8 slice VAE.

marks.label: Likelihood
marks.summary: Test ELBO −69.35 and BPD 0.953, against train ELBO −69.40 and BPD 0.953. The bound held on the 10,000 test images. A Gaussian decoder can report a decent BPD while the pictures stay soft, because the likelihood averages over stroke positions.

marks.label: Flow
marks.summary: Test log-det is −12.87 and train is −12.85. The flow is not an identity at the end of training: it rescales latent volume. KL stays near 19.5 on both splits. The sample picture is still a decode of N(0, I); the inverse flow is used in the posterior, not as the gallery generator.

marks.label: Prior samples
marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: The 64 prior samples cover 0–9 and a few ambiguous blobs. They are cleaner than the RealNVP inverse grid and softer than a sharp GAN. The flow fixed the posterior shape. It did not give the decoder a sharper pixel likelihood.

marks.label: Fashion-MNIST
marks.summary: Same hyperparameters, 20 epochs, full 60,000 / 10,000 split. Test ELBO is −65.00 and BPD is 0.945, against train ELBO −64.33 and BPD 0.944. Test MSE is 0.0621 and MAE is 0.1328; train is 0.0612 and 0.1315. KL is 12.95 and log-det is −9.07, so the couplings still change volume. Prior samples read as shirts, trousers, dresses, shoes, and bags. The shirt logo and the thin sandal do not survive.
marks.frameCaption: f-VAE prior samples on Fashion-MNIST. N(0, I) through the decoder.

reflection.worked: Reconstruction and the ELBO agree between train and test on both full splits. Digit samples cover many classes. Fashion samples cover shirts, trousers, dresses, shoes, and bags. Fashion’s test ELBO is −65.00 against −69.35 on digits, and its log-det of −9.07 shows the couplings are still doing work.
reflection.unexpected: Fashion’s better ELBO comes with a worse pixel error: test MSE 0.0621 and MAE 0.1328, against 0.0554 and 0.0920 on digits. The shirt print is wiped out, and the loss curve is still falling at epoch 20.
reflection.why: Squared error trains the decoder to average every stroke or weave that could explain a code. A wide silhouette survives that average; a logo and a sandal strap do not. Fashion’s KL is 12.95 against 19.51 on digits, so the higher ELBO is mostly a closer posterior, not a sharper picture. These samples never pass through the inverse flow.
reflection.improve: The loss is still descending at epoch 20, so a longer Fashion run is the next measurement, not a new latent size. If the goal is the shirt print, change the decoder likelihood. More coupling layers will not sharpen a Gaussian decoder by themselves.
